lessons.goal: 從對話與行動區分意見批評及人際否定。

questions.evidence: During a class meeting, Huan questions his friend Lea's plan to spend the whole activity budget on one large concert. He asks what would remain for students who prefer smaller workshops. Lea becomes quiet and avoids him after the meeting.
questions.explanation: 他擔心所有經費都用在同一活動。
options: Whether Lea worked hard.
The date of their friendship.
Whether music should ever be allowed.
Using the entire activity budget for one concert.

questions.evidence: Huan later says he likes the idea of a concert but is uncertain about using every available dollar. He suggests keeping part of the budget for other activities. Lea admits she had heard his question as a rejection of her effort, not as a concern about the plan.
questions.explanation: Lea 起初把方案疑慮理解成對付出的否定。
options: He refuses to explain his question.
The class has already chosen workshops only.
She hears his concern as a rejection of her effort.
He has canceled the concert himself.
questions.prompt: Why does Lea avoid Huan at first?

questions.evidence: They review the proposal together and prepare two versions with different spending patterns. The class can now compare trade-offs instead of choosing between total approval and total rejection. Lea still hopes for a concert, and Huan still wants room for workshops. Their friendship does not require identical opinions; it becomes easier when they explain what they are questioning and why.
questions.explanation: 他們提出兩個支出配置版本供比較。
options: A rule against workshops.
Two identical concert posters.
An apology without any budget discussion.
Two spending versions.

lessons.story:
During a class meeting, Huan questions his friend Lea's plan to spend the whole activity budget on one large concert. He asks what would remain for students who prefer smaller workshops. Lea becomes quiet and avoids him after the meeting.

Huan later says he likes the idea of a concert but is uncertain about using every available dollar. He suggests keeping part of the budget for other activities. Lea admits she had heard his question as a rejection of her effort, not as a concern about the plan.

They review the proposal together and prepare two versions with different spending patterns. The class can now compare trade-offs instead of choosing between total approval and total rejection. Lea still hopes for a concert, and Huan still wants room for workshops. Their friendship does not require identical opinions; it becomes easier when they explain what they are questioning and why.
lessons.title: Disagreeing with a Friend's Proposal
